title: Cross-language SDK dependency harmonization and API deprecation plan for legacy auth/telemetry fields
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Coordinate a single wave of dependency upgrades across Python, JavaScript, and Go client libraries and concurrently remove a set of legacy API surface fields used for older auth and telemetry integrations. Goals: 1) upgrade critical transitive deps (http clients, json libs, TLS) to mitigate security and stability alerts; 2) provide a staged deprecation for legacy request fields (legacy_x_api_key, telemetry_hint) with clear migration paths; 3) minimize churn for customers by providing compatibility shims, feature flags, and opt-in rollout; 4) validate performance/regression with benchmark harnesses and CI gates.
acceptance_criteria: All three language clients (python, js, go) have dependency matrix bumped to target versions and pass CI with integration tests
Compatibility shims implemented for legacy_x_api_key and telemetry_hint for at least one minor release cycle
Migration guides added to docs with code examples in all three languages
No P0 regressions in latency or memory in runtime-facing benchmarks (<= 5% deviation)
Canary rollout configured and run for hosted API clients; telemetry shows no spike in errors after opt-in removal
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Upgrading http client could change connection pooling semantics -> Mitigation: run extended integration job against staging with 24h traffic replay
Risk: Shims impose maintenance burden -> Mitigation: mark shims experimental, track removal deadline, add automated coverage
Risk: Customers rely on legacy telemetry_hint semantics -> Mitigation: provide server-side mapping + deprecation header and two-week overlap window
Risk: Breaking changelog noise across languages -> Mitigation: coordinated release notes and example diff PRs per-language
work_items: Audit current transitive dependency graph and produce minimal safe upgrade set
Draft deprecation RFC describing fields, timeline, and migration samples
Implement compatibility shims in python-client (auth adapter) and feature-flag server-side mapping
Update JS client transport layer to new http2-capable adapter and run perf benchmark
Replace Go client's JSON library usage in hot-paths and measure allocations
Add end-to-end integration tests that exercise legacy fields to validate shim behavior
Create docs page and example migrations for 3 languages and link in changelog
Coordinate canary with infra and run 48h traffic replay, collect errors/latency metrics
